A1-01.summary: Settle-to-zero departure posts an adjustment without any network-state gate, even on closed, closing, suspended or administrator-required networks, breaking the certified final export checksum after closure.
A1-01.scenario: Network with departure_rule=settle-to-zero is closed and its final export checksum recorded; during read-only period an active member calls DepartMember; adjustment posts, ledger_seq 1->2, VerifyClosureExport Match=false. Same while suspended and admin-required (closing variant LIKELY, not run).
A1-01.evidence: PoC tests TestA1PoC_01_SettleToZeroPostsAfterClosure, TestA1PoC_01b_SettleToZeroPostsWhileSuspended, TestA1PoC_01c_SettleToZeroPostsWhenAdminRequired in /home/user/audit/circula-a1/internal/service/a1_poc_test.go (tag a1poc); `go test -tags a1poc -count=1 -run 'TestA1PoC_01' -v ./internal/service/`; output shows DepartMember err=<nil> ledger_seq 1->2, closure export match=false, while CreateAdjustment control is refused.
A1-01.suggested_fix: In settleOnDeparture, when a settlement posting is needed, call p.requireNetworkActive() first and refuse (or fall back to retain only if the owner decides; spec gap G3); add regression tests for closed, closing, suspended, admin-required.

A1-02.summary: The decimals guard (LedgerSeq > 0) is checked only when a change is requested, so a decimals change scheduled with notice takes effect after postings exist and reinterprets all persisted amounts permanently.
A1-02.scenario: New network decimals 2, no postings; admin schedules decimals 0 with notice_days=14; members trade 25.00 (2500 minor); on day 15 decimals=0 with ledger_seq=1 and the payee's 2500 minor units read as 2500 credits; no way back.
A1-02.evidence: PoC TestA1PoC_02_ScheduledDecimalChangeAfterPosting (a1_poc_test.go, tag a1poc); control immediate change refused; output 'after notice: decimals=0 ledger_seq=1; payee balance 2500 minor units now reads 2500 credits'.
A1-02.known_ref: DOM-031/DAT-049 required unimplemented correction (related, known); scheduled bypass is new
A1-02.suggested_fix: Refuse any decimals change after network creation in both scheduled and immediate paths; interim: refuse decimals change in any future-effective version or re-validate at activation; update TestPolicyChanges.

A1-03.summary: A re-review posts a reversal on a trade that another live (serial) dispute holds as disputed, leaving a posting_pending dispute that can never post or close, or an open dispute on a reversed trade that cannot be withdrawn and no longer blocks closure or departure.
A1-03.scenario: (1) D1 dismissed, D2 upheld but LED-5-blocked to posting_pending 1000; re-review of D1 partially upheld 500 posts; RetryDisputePosting fails forever, ResolveDispute refused, trade stays disputed, departure blocked, network never closes. (2) D1 dismissed, D2 open, re-review of D1 upheld -> trade reversed with D2 open; withdraw fails; ScheduleClosure succeeds.
A1-03.evidence: PoC TestA1PoC_03_PostingPendingStuckAfterReReview and TestA1PoC_03b_OpenDisputeOnReversedTradeDoesNotBlockClosure (a1_poc_test.go, tag a1poc); outputs show Retry 'must be between 1 and the remaining reversible amount 5.00', Resolve refused, departure blocked, ScheduleClosure -> <nil>.
A1-03.suggested_fix: In decideReReview refuse posting while t.Status == TxDisputed (mirror DEC-052); in RetryDisputePosting use min(d.ReversalAmount, remaining) or refuse clearly; add live-dispute table to closureBlockers and departBlockers. Serial disputes is spec gap G1.

A1-04.summary: ResolveDispute and RetryDisputePosting post reversals in an administrator-required network because reverse() checks only Suspended(), unlike DecideReReview which applies the full gate.
A1-04.scenario: Network with no active administrator (set via raw SQL as in TestAdminRequiredReadOnly); a reviewer resolves an open dispute as upheld; reversal posts, ledger_seq 1->2, while proposals are refused with 'administrator required'. No service path found that reaches zero admins, hence Low.
A1-04.evidence: PoC TestA1PoC_04_ReversalPostsInAdminRequiredNetwork (a1_poc_test.go, tag a1poc): 'ResolveDispute upheld -> status resolved, ledger_seq 1 -> 2'.
A1-04.suggested_fix: Call networkOpenErr (or a dispute-specific variant permitting closing if the owner decides, gap G2) before reverse() in both functions.

A1-05.summary: The expiry sweep pages the oldest N expired proposals across all networks and skips frozen ones, so 500+ elapsed proposals in frozen networks starve every other network's expiry.
A1-05.scenario: A frozen network holds >=500 elapsed proposals; every run returns those same 500, expires 0 and the job stops; healthy networks' elapsed proposals never get status expired, audit event or history. No money effect (reservations respect expires_at).
A1-05.evidence: PoC TestA1PoC_05_ExpiryStarvedByFrozenNetwork with limit 2: 'run 0..2 expired 0; healthy network's elapsed proposal is still proposed'.
A1-05.suggested_fix: Filter frozen networks in SQL or keyset-paginate past skipped rows; skipped rows must not count toward the page.

A1-06.summary: Departure cancels only one page of 500 open proposals, leaving the rest proposed with a departed party and holding the counterparty's reservation until expiry.
A1-06.scenario: Member D has 501 open proposals with several counterparties; D departs; one proposal stays proposed, cannot be accepted, and keeps the payer's reservation until expiry.
A1-06.evidence: PoC TestA1PoC_06_DepartureLeavesProposalsBeyond500: 'after departure: 1 proposals still proposed; payer reserved 1'.
A1-06.suggested_fix: Loop until a page returns fewer than the limit, as finaliseOne does.

A1-07.summary: Closure commits closed status in one unit and writes the final export in later units; if the export fails once, the closure is never listed again so no final checksum is ever recorded.
A1-07.scenario: Crash or error between finaliseOne commit and recordFinalExport leaves a closed network with empty final_sha256; ListClosures(pending) lists only closed_at=0, so later runs never retry; VerifyClosureExport permanently says no completed closure with final export.
A1-07.evidence: PoC TestA1PoC_07_FinalExportNeverRetried injecting failure on export audit write: first run err=injected status=closed; second run finalised=0 err=<nil>; VerifyClosureExport -> invalid-transaction-state.
A1-07.suggested_fix: Have FinaliseClosures also pick closures with closed_at <> 0 AND final_sha256 = '', or record a final-export-pending marker.

A1-08.summary: OperatorSetDualControl writes policy version effective+1, which collides with an already scheduled future version, so the operator cannot change the threshold while any policy change is pending.
A1-08.scenario: Admin schedules an adverse change with 14-day notice; `circula dual-control` fails with 'conflict: duplicate record' until the change takes effect or is cancelled; the scheduled JSON would otherwise ignore the operator change.
A1-08.suggested_fix: Use LatestPolicyVersion+1 and either refuse explicitly while a change is pending or apply the threshold to the pending version too.

A1-09.summary: Reversal transactions posted by a dispute decision, retry or re-review have no audit event targeting the reversal id; only the dispute is the target.
A1-09.scenario: An auditor filters the audit log by a dispute-posted reversal transaction id and finds no events, unlike the admin reversal path which writes transaction.reversed with TargetID rev.ID.
A1-09.suggested_fix: Emit transaction.reversed for the reversal in the same unit, or add the reversal id to the dispute event's After summary.

A1-10.summary: ExpirePendingAdjustments writes status changes and audit events into frozen networks, whereas proposal expiry and closure finalisation skip frozen networks.
A1-10.scenario: A network is frozen after failed verification; pending adjustment expiry still marks a request expired and appends an audit row, extending the audit chain of the frozen network.
A1-10.suggested_fix: Skip frozen networks as ExpireProposals does (after fixing A1-05 paging).

A1-11.summary: FR-005 and GOV-004 are marked built although creation-time decimals immutability is unimplemented, and TestPolicyChanges asserts the non-conforming behaviour.
A1-11.scenario: After network creation an admin changes decimals 2 to 3 (no postings yet) and it succeeds; TestPolicyChanges asserts this success; A1-02 shows even the interim after-first-posting guard can be bypassed.
A1-11.evidence: Code and test read: status tables vs body notes (FR-005 implementation note, GOV-004 'Current checkpoint gap'); networks.go:242; admin_test.go:186-195 TestPolicyChanges. No PoC.
A1-11.suggested_fix: Set both rows to 'required unimplemented correction' until the A1-02 fix lands, and invert TestPolicyChanges.

A2-01.summary: Case-variant duplicate JSON keys pass the duplicate check (last spelling wins) and wrongly-cased field names are accepted instead of refused as unknown.
A2-01.scenario: POST /api/v1/transactions with amount_minor:"100" and AMOUNT_MINOR:"7" returns 201 with amount 7; {"KIND":"offer","Title":"bike"} creates a listing; a proxy/WAF reading the first key sees 100 (parser differential).
A2-01.evidence: PoC TestA2_CaseVariantDuplicateKeysAccepted in /home/user/audit/circula-a2/internal/api/zz_a2_poc_test.go; go test ./internal/api -run TestA2_CaseVariantDuplicateKeysAccepted -v -> case-variant 201 amount 7, exact duplicate 400, wrongly cased 201.
A2-01.suggested_fix: Compare lower-cased keys in checkDuplicateKeys and reject keys not exactly matching a struct tag (or use case-sensitive json v2); add cases to TestStrictBodyHandling.

A2-02.summary: A token restricted to one network lists the person's other tokens (with other network ids), revokes them, and changes the person-wide time zone.
A2-02.scenario: alice's write token scoped to acme: GET /tokens shows token for network 'other' with its network_id; DELETE /tokens/{id} of that token 204; PATCH /me changes time zone 200.
A2-02.evidence: PoC TestA2_NetworkScopedTokenActsOnWholePerson (internal/api/zz_a2_poc_test.go): scoped GET /tokens 200 mentions other network id; DELETE 204; PATCH /me 200.
A2-02.suggested_fix: Restrict ListAPITokens/RevokeAPIToken to same NetworkID when actor.NetworkScope set (or 403 token management for scoped tokens); refuse SetTimeZone for scoped tokens; add test.

A2-03.summary: The replay cache is keyed only by person+key, so a read-only token (or demoted admin) replays a cached write response such as a plaintext invitation token.
A2-03.scenario: Admin creates invitation with write token and Idempotency-Key inv-key-0001-abcdef; same person's read-only token sends same key and gets 201 Idempotent-Replayed: true with the invitation token (fresh key would be 403).
A2-03.evidence: PoC TestA2_ReplayIgnoresScopeAndRole (internal/api/zz_a2_poc_test.go) -> read-only replay 201 Idempotent-Replayed=true with same invitation token.
A2-03.suggested_fix: Store credential scope/token or session id with the record and refuse replay when actor lacks write scope or differs, or re-run a cheap authorisation check before replay; do not cache credential-bearing responses.

A2-04.summary: A break-glass grant-admin administrator is refused by every web admin page and by API adminOnly pre-checks, while the service accepts them.
A2-04.scenario: Operator break-glass grant-admin for alice: API POST /admin/invitations 201 and GET /admin/members 200, but GET /n/town/admin web pages 403 and API GET /admin/policy, /admin/audit-events 403.
A2-04.suggested_fix: Expose a service read of effective membership (stored plus break-glass roles plus MFA-missing flag) used by netH and resolveNetwork, or drop adapter pre-checks and let the service decide.

A2-05.summary: GET /admin/consistency-checks/{id} and GET /admin/policy are authorised only by the adapter role check, so an admin without the mandatory second factor can read them.
A2-05.scenario: require-mfa-admins on; admin2 without MFA: POST check 403, GET /admin/members 403, but GET /admin/consistency-checks/{id} 200 and GET /admin/policy 200.
A2-05.suggested_fix: Route both reads through service methods calling requireAdmin (e.g. Service.AdminGetPolicy, Service.RequireAdmin before job store read); add to authorisation matrix.

A2-06.summary: POST /logout ignores a failed session revocation, reports 'You are signed out.' and clears the cookie while the server session stays valid.
A2-06.scenario: RevokeSession returns SQLITE_BUSY during logout; page says signed out, but a replayed copy of the cookie still gets GET /n/town 200.
A2-06.evidence: PoC TestA2_LogoutFailureLeavesSessionValid (internal/web/zz_a2_poc_test.go) with store wrapper forcing SQLITE_BUSY.
A2-06.suggested_fix: On error render 503 'Not signed out. Try again.' and keep the cookie (or retry), log the error; add fault-injection test.

A2-07.summary: Credit-limit and policy ETags omit the override/expiry and scheduled policy changes, so a stale If-Match succeeds and silently undoes another admin's change.
A2-07.scenario: Override with expiry keeps ETag e7bd5c3d...; second admin's stale PUT credit_limit_minor:null removes it (200). Scheduled adverse policy change keeps ETag; stale no-op PATCH 200 cancels pending change.
A2-07.suggested_fix: Include override presence/value/expiry in limit ETag; derive policy ETag from latest policy version row incl. pending state; carry expected version into the service write unit.

A2-08.summary: Runtime 423 network-frozen, 429, 503 busy and some 413/415 statuses are not documented in openapi.yaml, so kin-openapi validation rejects them.
A2-08.scenario: Frozen network POST /listings -> 423 and rate-limited GET /network -> 429 fail OpenAPI validation 'status is not supported'; 423 documented on 0/85 ops, 429 missing on 46, 503 on 81.
A2-08.evidence: PoC TestA2_UndocumentedRuntimeStatuses (internal/contract/zz_a2_poc_test.go) plus Python tally over openapi.yaml.
A2-08.suggested_fix: Add shared 423/429/503/413/415 responses to every operation; add four emitted codes to 07 section 7.2; extend contract test with frozen, busy and rate-limited cases.

A2-09.summary: GET /network/policy-log returns every version and GET /challenges up to 200 rows, both with next_cursor null, ignoring limit, cursor and status.
A2-09.scenario: After 104 policy updates GET /network/policy-log?limit=5 returns 105 rows, next_cursor nil; /challenges?status=bogus -> 200.
A2-09.suggested_fix: Keyset-paginate both, validate status, call c.only; or cap at 100 and record a deviation in 07 section 12.

A2-10.summary: /n/{slug}/join tells any signed-in person whether a slug exists and shows the name of an invitation-only network, while other /n/{slug} pages answer 404.
A2-10.scenario: eve registers: /n/town -> 404, /n/no-such-net/join -> 404, /n/town/join -> 200 'Net town is invitation only'.
A2-10.suggested_fix: For invite (and closed/setup) networks answer like an unknown slug (404); show join page only for approval/open networks.

A2-11.summary: Sections hidden from a suspended or departed member's navigation still answer 200 by URL.
A2-11.scenario: Suspended alice gets 200 on /disputes and /policy; departed bob gets 200 on /trades, /disputes, /policy.
A2-11.suggested_fix: Align nav with what the service allows (show readable sections) or refuse in handlers; add nav-versus-reachability test per membership state.

A2-12.summary: A re-review decision posting a reversal is recorded on first submit with no review step, and dual-control 'Approve and post' also posts without a review screen.
A2-12.scenario: Submitting rereview-decide outcome=upheld once posts the reversal and changes alice's balance with no review page.
A2-12.suggested_fix: Route rereview-decide through the resolve review/confirm pattern (dispute_decide_review.html); add confirm screen for Approve and post showing resulting balance.

A2-13.summary: Frozen-network notice and admin overview last-check line display escaped <time datetime=...> markup as text.
A2-13.scenario: Admin overview shows 'The last ledger check passed. <time datetime=...>...'; every member page of a frozen network shows raw markup in the notice.
A2-13.suggested_fix: Pass the time as a separate template.HTML field (like FrozenSince) or format plain text.

A2-14.summary: Custom qs (url.QueryEscape) inside href is escaped again by html/template, so the double-encoded next fails SafeNext and invitation sign-in lands on '/'.
A2-14.scenario: Signed-out person opens invitation link, clicks Sign in (/login?next=%252Fjoin%252Finv_...), signs in, lands on / without the invitation.
A2-14.evidence: PoC TestA2_InviteLinkNextDoubleEncoded (internal/web/zz_a2_poc_test.go): hidden next empty, landed on /.
A2-14.suggested_fix: Use {{.Next}} directly in href or built-in urlquery; add a test following the rendered link.

A2-15.summary: /static/*, /robots.txt and /favicon.ico are Cache-Control: public yet carry a fresh Set-Cookie cm_csrf pre-login CSRF secret.
A2-15.scenario: A shared cache storing /static/style.css with Set-Cookie hands one pre-login CSRF secret to many clients (login CSRF still blocked by Origin check).
A2-15.suggested_fix: Skip ensureCSRF for static/robots/favicon or mark them Cache-Control: private.

A2-16.summary: Path ids reach the store unvalidated; SQL is parameterised so not exploitable, but SEC-024 requires rejection before any database call.
A2-16.evidence: PoC TestA2_IdentifierReachesStoreUnvalidated (internal/api/zz_a2_poc_test.go) with recording store wrapper.
A2-16.suggested_fix: Add one validID (UUID) check in adapters' path handling on both surfaces returning uniform 404; add test.

A2-17.summary: A person who must change their password can still load '/' and '/join/{token}' instead of being redirected.
A2-17.suggested_fix: Apply the MustChangePassword redirect in both handlers (use s.auth).

A2-18.summary: invalid-body problem detail echoes Go internals and several reads ignore unknown query parameters.
A2-18.scenario: Number for amount_minor yields detail 'cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field proposeReq.amount_minor of type string'; GET /network?bogus=1, /accounts/me?foo=1, /network/policy-log?limit=abc return 200.
A2-18.suggested_fix: Rewrite detail as 'amount_minor: must be a string'; reject unknown query parameters with invalid-query.

A2-19.summary: OpenAPI declares an optional Idempotency-Key on POST /tokens but the route ignores it, so a retry with the same key mints a second credential.
A2-19.scenario: Two POST /tokens with the same Idempotency-Key return two 201s with different ids and no Idempotent-Replayed.
A2-19.evidence: PoC TestA2_TokenCreateIgnoresIdempotencyKey (internal/api/zz_a2_poc_test.go); Python check of idempotency declarations vs route flags.
A2-19.known_ref: A3-09 (doc mismatch left by its fix)
A2-19.suggested_fix: Document no idempotency, or replay metadata without the secret / 409 for repeated key.

A2-20.summary: The web reference shown to users is a second random id unrelated to the access-log request_id, and the API stores a client-chosen X-Request-Id in audit events.
A2-20.scenario: Support cannot match a user's page Reference to the access log line; an API client can choose or duplicate request ids recorded in the audit chain.
A2-20.evidence: Code trace through cmd/circula/ops_http.go observe and web/API middleware; not executed, no PoC.
A2-20.suggested_fix: Web reuses the edge request id; generate server-side ids for audit and keep client id as separate correlation field.

A2-21.summary: API tokens and session ids are stored as plain unsalted, unkeyed SHA-256 whereas the spec requires a salted or keyed hash.
A2-21.scenario: A leaked token-hash list allows offline confirmation of a candidate token (256-bit tokens make practical risk negligible).
A2-21.evidence: Code reading of hashToken; no PoC.
A2-21.suggested_fix: Use a keyed hash (HMAC with a server key).

A3-F01.summary: With backup-encryption-key set, the pre-migration gate runs integrity_check on the .db.enc ciphertext, so circula migrate and serve (migrate-mode=auto) can never migrate an encrypted deployment.
A3-F01.scenario: Operator configures backup-encryption-key-file then upgrades; circula migrate writes encrypted pre-migration backup, opens ciphertext as SQLite, gets 'file is not a database (26)' and refuses; removing the key leaves a plaintext pre-migration backup contrary to OPS-019/SEC-028 and backup-restore.md:32.
A3-F01.evidence: PoCs TestA3Audit_MigrateWithEncryptionKey and TestA3Audit_PreMigrationSafeguardEncrypted in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/cmd/circula/a3audit_poc_test.go; run go test -count=1 -run 'TestA3Audit_' -v ./cmd/circula; error 'pre-migration backup ...db.enc did not verify; migrations not applied: integrity check ... file is not a database (26)'. No existing test runs migrate with an encryption key.
A3-F01.suggested_fix: In verifyPreMigrationBackup, when m.Encrypted, decrypt to a private temp file, check plaintext digest against signed PlaintextSHA256, run integrity_check on the temp copy, then remove it (or rely on in-memory decrypt proof plus ciphertext re-hash); add migrate-with-encryption regression test.

A3-F02.location: internal/service/principal.go:25, internal/service/dualcontrol.go:27, internal/service/adjustments.go:79, internal/service/membership.go:275, internal/service/recovery.go:326, internal/service/reversal.go:24, internal/service/join.go:278, internal/service/suspend.go:52
A3-F02.summary: Break-glass 'no lasting changes' rule (requireLasting) covers only about 10 methods, so a break-glass admin can post adjustments, approve dual-control requests immediately, raise limits, reset passwords, reverse trades and decide disputes.
A3-F02.scenario: Operator grants break-glass admin to member X; within the session X credits an accomplice via adjustment, approves founder's pending 50,000.00 request seconds after grant (no 24 h wait), sets a credit limit to platform max, resets a member's password (temp password still works after session expiry), reverses a completed trade; all outlive the session.
A3-F02.evidence: PoCs TestA3Audit_BreakGlassLastingChanges (4 sub-tests) and TestA3Audit_BreakGlassApprovesImmediately in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/internal/service/a3audit_poc_test.go; go test -count=1 -run 'TestA3Audit_' -v ./internal/service; outputs e.g. 'set ben's credit limit to 1125899906842624 with no expiry', 'approved the founder's 50,000.00 request seconds after the grant'. Existing tests TestA3_02_*, TestBreakGlassCannotMakeLastingChanges cover only the narrowed set.
A3-F02.known_ref: partly: SEC-013 addendum Not done #4, SA2-04, A3-02b, SEC-011-owner-decision.md:66
A3-F02.suggested_fix: Call p.requireLasting() in every persistent write path (ledger postings/approvals, limits, credentials, membership decisions, network suspension, invitations, announcements) or invert to an allow-list; remove the bgAdmin early return in requireIndependentApprover (refuse instead).

A3-F16.summary: Second-factor throttle is renewable by one failure at expiry and is shared with session-only DisableMFA, so a stolen session keeps the owner out of MFA sign-in indefinitely.
A3-F16.scenario: Attacker with stolen session of MFA user makes 5 garbage DisableMFA calls, then one per 15 min; the owner with correct password and code gets rate-limited at every sign-in and cannot change password to revoke the session.
A3-F16.evidence: PoC TestA3Audit_StolenSessionLocksOwnerOutOfMFA in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/internal/service/a3audit_poc_test.go; go test -count=1 -run 'TestA3Audit_' -v ./internal/service; 3 rounds each 'owner with the right password and code is refused: rate-limited: too many attempts'.
A3-F16.known_ref: counter sharing documented in SEC-007 addendum; renewable lock is A3-02a pattern (fixed for login keys only); new
A3-F16.suggested_fix: Apply readThrottle decay/half-allowance to mfaReserve and reserveAttempt; use a separate key for session-only management calls; verify password in DisableMFA before touching shared counter.

A3-F03.summary: require-mfa-admins is not applied to admin powers reached through requireDecider, so an admin without a second factor resolves disputes and decides challenges.
A3-F03.scenario: With require-mfa-admins=true and an unenrolled admin, an attacker with only the password is refused CreateInvitation but resolves a dispute 'upheld' (reversal posted) and decides challenges.
A3-F03.evidence: PoC TestA3Audit_MFAForAdminsBypassViaDecider in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/internal/service/a3audit_poc_test.go; control CreateInvitation refused mfa-enrolment-required, then 'administrator without the mandatory second factor resolved dispute ... reversal posted'.
A3-F03.suggested_fix: In requireDecider, when decider standing comes from admin role and p.mfaMissing, refuse with mfa-enrolment-required; reviewers without admin role stay exempt.

A3-F05.summary: Erasure leaves the member's challenge text (challenges.reason) and the login in 'recover: <login>' throttle rows.
A3-F05.scenario: Removed member files a challenge containing a phone number then uses 'erase my data'; challenge text survives; a failed /recover leaves 'recover: ana@example.org' rows until purge.
A3-F05.evidence: PoC TestA3Audit_ErasureLeftovers in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/internal/service/a3audit_poc_test.go; 'member-written challenge text survives erasure in [challenges.reason]', 'erased login survives in [login_throttle.login]'.
A3-F05.suggested_fix: Clear challenges.reason for the target member (treat requested challenge as blocker or close it); delete recoverKey(login) family too; extend TestAnonymiseMemberKeepsLedger.

A3-F06.summary: DeleteThrottleFamily compares a Go byte length with SQLite character substr, so per-address throttle rows of non-ASCII logins are never removed.
A3-F06.scenario: józef01 is locked out from his address; operator runs circula unlock -login józef01; per-address row survives and he is still refused; same miss in resets, recovery, OperatorUnlockLogin, erasure.
A3-F06.evidence: PoC TestA3Audit_UnlockNonASCIILogin in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/internal/service/a3audit_poc_test.go; 'after circula unlock (cleared 1 row(s)) the person is still locked out: rate-limited'; ASCII control passes.
A3-F06.suggested_fix: Compare bytes (substr(CAST(login AS BLOB),1,?) = CAST(? AS BLOB)) or use range login >= key||' ' AND login < key||'!'.

A3-F09.summary: Restore resurrects sessions and API tokens revoked after the backup (and, by trace, closed break-glass sessions), and the documented remedy (password change) leaves tokens valid.
A3-F09.scenario: Member revokes a leaked API token on Tuesday; operator restores Monday's backup; logged-out session and leaked token work again up to 90 days; a break-glass session closed after backup is live again.
A3-F09.evidence: PoC TestA3Audit_RestoreResurrectsRevokedSession in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/cmd/circula/a3audit_poc_test.go; 'session revoked after the backup authenticates again after restore'. Break-glass part by trace (LIKELY).
A3-F09.known_ref: partly SA-07 (proposed revoke all on restore, not implemented, not tracked)
A3-F09.suggested_fix: In restore swap revoke all sessions and API tokens and close open break-glass sessions, recorded in database.restored event; or default with flag to keep them.

A3-F10.summary: Backup schedule and retention trust the timestamp in backup file names, so one future-dated backup stops scheduled backups for years and is always retained.
A3-F10.scenario: Clock briefly set to 2036 for one backup run; after correction next scheduled backup is 10 years away, the bogus file is always kept and real ones pruned; nothing logs the anomaly.
A3-F10.evidence: PoC TestA3Audit_FutureDatedBackupStopsSchedule in /home/user/audit/circula-a3/cmd/circula/a3audit_poc_test.go; 'next scheduled backup waits 87696h0m0s (about 3653 days)'; with keep-daily 2 only 1 real backup kept.
A3-F10.suggested_fix: Ignore and log entries dated beyond a tolerance after now when scheduling; base retention on manifest time bounded by now.

A3-F11.summary: circula dual-control fails with 'conflict: duplicate record' while a policy change waits out its notice because both use version in-force+1.

  w.Clock.Advance(15 * 24 * time.Hour)

  n = w.netNow()
  t.Logf("after effect: err=%v version=%d threshold=%d limit=%d", err, n.PolicyVersion, n.Policy.DualControlThreshold, n.Policy.DefaultCreditLimit)
}

When the request lacks a 32-character cm_csrf (or __Host-cm_csrf over HTTPS) cookie, ensureCSRF (session.go:71-79) sets a fresh one. middleware.go:54-56 then overrides Cache-Control to 'public, max-age=3600' for /static/. web.go:85-93 sets 'public, max-age=86400' for /favicon.ico and 'public, max-age=3600' for /robots.txt. No Vary header is sent and there is no 'private' or no-cache="Set-Cookie". In ordinary browsing the HTML page is fetched first and same-site subresource requests then carry the cookie, so Set-Cookie appears on static responses only for cookie-less fetches, such as a first direct hit or a cache that fills from origin without forwarding cookies. Whether a shared cache stores such responses depends on the deployment; RFC 9111 permits it. The shipped deploy/compose.yaml has no cache layer. Impact check: a second client replaying the shared secret gets valid pre-login tokens from /login, but a cross-origin POST /login is still refused (403) by sameOrigin (middleware.go:73-93); only same-origin or Origin-less posts pass. SEC-004 and SEC-023 neither require nor forbid this, so this is a hardening item: Info.

impact.rationale:
A1-01 is a real defect at bb5a36f, and Medium is the right severity.

CODE PATH
- DepartMember (internal/service/departure.go:23-99) opens with write scope at :26. That open (principal.go:38-52) checks only the password-change flag and the operator freeze (:46-50).
- Nothing on the path calls requireNetworkActive or networkOpenErr (principal.go:113-131). settleOnDeparture (:129-158) calls postAdjustment (adjustments.go:157-185), which calls postTx (posting.go:40-87). None of them check the network state.
- The other posting paths do check it: createAdjustment (adjustments.go:90), ReverseTransaction (reversal.go:35) and ApproveAdjustment (dualcontrol.go:91).
- lifecycle (closure_schedule.go:41-55) works out closing and admin-required, but departure never looks at either.
- The code says what it intended. EraseClosedNetworks (closure_schedule.go:360-363) describes a departure after closure as "a status change only: no settlement, no ledger entry".

REPRODUCED in my own worktree, /home/user/audit/verify-circula/A1-01-impact (now removed):
- The A1 PoC tests TestA1PoC_01, 01b and 01c fail as reported. DepartMember returns err=nil and ledger_seq goes 1->2. After closure, VerifyClosureExport gives Match=false. The CreateAdjustment controls are refused.
- Extra probes I wrote:
  - **Closing state:** now confirmed (A1 had it as LIKELY). Propose and adjust are refused with "network is closing", but the departure posts (1->2). The checksum still matches after finalising, because the settlement lands inside the certified export.
  - **Platform suspension (GOV-024, security_incident):** the departure posts.
  - **Admin removal after closure:** an admin with dual control at its default of 0 removes a member. The posting goes through, the member's +500 balance becomes 0, and the checksum no longer matches.
  - **Retain rule:** departure after closure posts nothing and the checksum matches. So the settlement posting is the defect, not departure itself.
  - **Irreversible after closure:** reversing the settlement is refused ("network is closed"). Re-running FinaliseClosures finalises 0 networks, Match stays false, VerifyLedger stays OK, and the adjustment is audited.
  - **End to end through the API:** POST /api/v1/me/membership/departure on a closed network returns 200 with settlement=settled and ledger_seq 2, and the checksum match is false.
- No adapter blocks the call:
  - Web leave: h_gov.go:18-19, :246-266; the netH wrapper is session.go:198-233.
  - API: routes.go:31 and h_core.go:156-176.
  - Admin remove: web h_admin.go:203-204 and api h_admin.go:133-134.
  - The web banners (render.go:245-258) tell members that nothing that moves value is possible.

SEVERITY
Who can trigger it:
- Any active or individually suspended member, through the standard Leave page or the API.
- Any administrator who is not a break-glass administrator, through removal. This has no cap when dual control is off (the default 0); otherwise it is capped at the threshold (departure.go:143).

Preconditions:
- The network uses the non-default departure_rule=settle-to-zero.
- The network is closing, closed, suspended (by an administrator or the platform) or administrator-required.
- The member's balance is not zero.
- The operator freeze (CMD-07) does block it.

Blast radius:
- One network only.
- Per departure, one member's balance moves to or from the system account: the member's own balance, or the removed member's balance in an admin removal.
- LED-1 holds and the entries are appended and audited, so it is detectable.
- No auth bypass, no cross-tenant access, no transfer to another member, no vote effect. That rules out Critical.
- The value moved is what the network's chosen rule would move in an active network. The write-off without approval is A3-07's concern, which is owner-pending.

What A1-01 adds:
- It bypasses the P0 freeze controls of GOV-020, GOV-023, GOV-024 and GOV-025 b (FR-068 is P1), including an operator-imposed platform suspension that administrators cannot lift.
- After closure it invalidates the GOV-025 e certified final checksum permanently: the ledger is append-only, closure is terminal, reversal is refused and the checksum is never re-recorded.
- In the suspended and admin-required states, an administrator can reverse the settlement once the network is active again, because ReverseTransaction does not check the party's status. The departure itself stays.

Ordinary members can reach it through the normal UI and API, it violates P0 requirements, and the closure damage is permanent, so it is above Low. The non-default rule, the uncommon network states, the bounded amount and the full audit trail keep it below High.

FIX
The suggested fix is sound: call p.requireNetworkActive() in settleOnDeparture, only when a posting is needed. Whether departure in a frozen state should then be refused or fall back to retain is spec gap G3 and needs an owner decision. Under either choice, no posting may happen.

impact.rationale:
A1-02 is a real defect at bb5a36f9, and Medium is the right severity. I reproduced it in my own detached worktree with new probes in the service and API packages; the worktree has since been removed.

Mechanism:
- UpdatePolicy checks decimals only when the change is requested: `in.Policy.Decimals != p.net.Policy.Decimals && p.net.LedgerSeq > 0` (internal/service/networks.go:242).
- With a notice period, the new version is stored with a future effective_at (networks.go:258-291, AppendPolicyNotice at :280). The notice comes from an explicit notice_days, or from the 14-day default when the same request also changes something adverse (networks.go:339-357; domain/terms.go:40-46).
- When the date arrives, the version becomes effective because of the as-of filter in networkSelect (internal/store/sqlite_network.go:27-32, driven by service.go:177-183). Nothing re-checks LedgerSeq at that point.

What I observed:
- PATCH /api/v1/admin/policy with {decimals:0, notice_days:14} returned 200 with a pending version.
- After a 2500-minor trade and 15 days, the network shows decimals=0 with ledger_seq=1. /accounts/me reports balance_minor 2500 with decimals 0 (2500 credits, where it was 25.00).
- VerifyLedger still reports OK, because no stored integer changed.
- Changing decimals back is refused on both paths, immediate and scheduled ("cannot change after the first posting"). network_policies cannot be updated or deleted (0001_init.sql:308-311), and the only operator policy command sets the dual-control threshold only (dualcontrol_operator.go:20-48). So the product has no way back.
- Trades made after the switch use the new scale, so the ledger ends up holding amounts at two scales. No single decimals value then reads every entry correctly.
- A version that changes decimals 2→0 and lowers the default limit from 10000 to 100 was scheduled with no notice_days at all. After it took effect, the payer stood at -2500 against a limit of 100, and the payee spent 2600 credits; before the switch that payee's whole spending power was 125.00.
- The 0→4 direction with 90 days' notice also works: 50 credits became 0.0050.
- The historical balance added at this SHA reports the current decimals for past instants (histbal.go:53), although API-083 promises decimals that never change.

Severity reasoning:
- It breaks the P0 rules FR-005, GOV-004, DOM-031 and DAT-049, which forbid any decimals change after the network is created. It also defeats the remaining as-built protection: the comment at networks.go:215-216 and TRACEABILITY say "Decimals locked after first posting".
- Every balance, limit, price and open proposal in the network changes meaning, and the mixed scale cannot be undone through the product.
- It is not Critical: only a network administrator can trigger it, it stays inside one network, there is no auth bypass, and no stored amounts change.
- It is not High, for these reasons:
  - The change has to be scheduled before the network's first posting.
  - It is reachable only through the JSON API. The web policy form keeps the current decimals (h_admin2.go:59-103), and the template says decimals cannot be changed.

impact.rationale:
I reproduced this at bb5a36f in my own detached worktree, which I have since removed. Both original PoCs fail, meaning the behaviour the spec requires is missing. My own probes also reproduce it with the production default windows (response 7 days, dispute 30, re-review 14) and no waivers.

Root cause:
- A second dispute can be opened after the first is dismissed (disputes.go:52). The dispute_live index (0001_init.sql:211-212) only stops two disputes being live at the same time.
- decideReReview posts through reverse() (disputes_response.go:274-281). reverse() accepts a disputed trade (reversal.go:90) and never checks for another live dispute. The admin path does refuse disputed trades (reversal.go:48).
- RetryDisputePosting re-posts the amount frozen at decision time, d.ReversalAmount (disputes_decide.go:188).
- posting_pending can only be left through retry_post (statemachine.go:169-171). ResolveDispute refuses it (disputes_decide.go:100-101).
- Withdrawal needs the trade to be disputed so it can return to completed (disputes.go:197).
- closureBlockers and departBlockers look only at the transaction status (closure.go:13-23, departure.go:161-169). erasureBlockers also checks live disputes (erasure.go:171-190).

Verified effects:
- S1: dispute D2 stays posting_pending at 10.00 after the re-review posts 5.00. Retry is refused even after a 1,000,000 limit override, whether a reviewer or the admin tries. Resolve, withdraw, admin ReverseTransaction and a re-review of D2 are all refused.
  - Both parties' departure is blocked and ScheduleClosure stays blocked indefinitely.
  - If a closure was already scheduled, the network stays `closing` (frozen). FinaliseClosures still returns 0 a year later, and CancelClosure is refused (closure_schedule.go:148-150).
  - The payer never receives the remaining 5.00 of an upheld decision.
- S1', a variant not in the finding: the override is applied, then a full re-review posts before the retry. D2 stays posting_pending on a reversed trade for good.
  - Departure and ScheduleClosure both succeed.
  - The departed payer's EraseMyData is blocked permanently.
- S2: the opener cannot withdraw, and departure and ScheduleClosure succeed. A reviewer can still dismiss the dispute, so S2 can be recovered.

Extra blast radius, not in the finding:
- When such a network has closed and its 90-day read-only period is over, EraseClosedNetworks fails with "anonymisation is blocked" and returns early (closure_schedule.go:382-383).
- Closures are processed in network_id order (sqlite_closure.go:78), and production ids are UUIDv7. So erasure also stalls for every closed network created later. My test confirmed an unrelated second network was not erased.
- In S1' this is permanent, because the first erasure run already departed the admin. In S2 it clears once a still-active reviewer dismisses the dispute.
- The data is kept longer than it should be; it is not exposed.

Why not higher:
- No value is created or destroyed. VerifyLedger is OK in every variant and the cumulative cap holds.
- There is no authorisation bypass and no cross-tenant exposure.
- No single attacker can drive it. It needs serial disputes, a re-review request and two independent reviewers deciding in a specific order, and in S1 a payee close to the limit.
- Operators can see it and repair it in the database.

Why not lower:
- It happens through ordinary use with default policy.
- There is no recovery path in the product.
- It permanently blocks two members' departure and erasure and the network's closure.
- An upheld decision can never be fully posted.

On the finding as written:
- DEC-052's text covers only administrative reversal, and the re-review is itself a dispute decision. Its rationale applies, but the firmer basis is DEC-039.
- In S2, DOM-024's letter does not list an open dispute on a reversed trade as a departure blocker. The breach of DOM-024's letter is in S1' only; the FR-068 breach is in both S2 and S1'.

impact.rationale:
I confirmed the defect at bb5a36f. It happens every time and cannot be bypassed. I agree with the reported severity of Medium.

How it happens:
- When backup-encryption-key is set, backupTo (cmd/circula/serve.go:318-340) names the backup *.db.enc (snapshot.go:427-432). snapshotWith writes the CIRCBK1 ciphertext (snapshot.go:282-300), and the manifest's sha256 and bytes then describe the ciphertext (snapshot.go:301-315).
- verifyPreMigrationBackup (premigrate.go:39-64) passes the checksum, signature, recorded-integrity and schema checks. It then runs integrityCheck(ctx, path) on that ciphertext at premigrate.go:56. store.IntegrityCheck (internal/store/inspect.go:154-165) opens it as SQLite and gets "file is not a database (26)".
- Both supported migration paths reach this check: `circula migrate` (commands.go:126-131) and `serve` with migrate-mode=auto (serve.go:116-124 -> 302-313 -> premigrate.go:16-35).
- Restore takes the right approach: it decrypts first and only then runs the integrity check (commands.go:294-325). That is why only the migration gate breaks.

What I reproduced in my own detached worktree (since removed). The auditor's two PoCs fail exactly as described.
- `migrate -backup-encryption-key-file` on a v1 database exits 1. The schema stays at v1 with 14 migrations pending. One valid encrypted pre-migration backup is left behind, and its ciphertext still matches its manifest.
- runServe in auto mode refuses to start. Each further start attempt writes another full backup: there were 2 after 2 attempts.
- The only way round it inside the product is to remove the key. Migration then succeeds but leaves a plaintext circula-*.db in backup-dir that has the SQLite header and the password_hash values.
- If backup-require-encryption=true is set explicitly, removing the key is a configuration error (exit 2), so the operator has to change two settings.
- A manual `circula backup` with the key works.

Impact:
- Any deployment that turns on the backup encryption OPS-019/SEC-028 require cannot apply any migration through a supported path. There are 15 migrations so far, and security fixes ship as migrations (CONTINUATION.md:38 shows the security-branch balance-bound migration as 0015).
- The workaround breaks OPS-019/SEC-028 and the promise in backup-restore.md:32-33 that pre-migration backups are encrypted.
- Aggravating factor: with migrate-mode=auto and the shipped deploy/circula.service (Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5s), each restart writes another full backup. Retention pruning never runs because serve never starts, so backup-dir keeps growing until the operator steps in. This only applies to auto mode, which is not the default, and hosted deployments must use explicit mode (OPS-025).

Why Medium and not higher or lower:
- Not Critical or High: the failure is fail-closed. The database is left unchanged at its old version and the old binary keeps working, so it is reversible. There is no loss to the ledger or votes, no authentication bypass, no cross-tenant exposure, and no attacker can trigger it. A manual workaround exists: rely on the encrypted manual backup from upgrade.md step 3, migrate without the key, then delete the plaintext pre-migration backup.
- Not Low: it blocks a P0 upgrade path for every deployment that follows the spec, it contradicts the operator docs, and the workaround costs confidentiality.

No accepted spec, decision or addendum permits this behaviour, and it is unrelated to the owner-pending items A3-04, A3-07, A3-10 and A3-11.

2. **The other actions are an open owner decision, recorded in an accepted addendum.**

impact.rationale:
Confirmed at bb5a36f. The auditor's PoCs reproduce in a fresh detached worktree: all 4 sub-tests of TestA3Audit_BreakGlassLastingChanges plus TestA3Audit_BreakGlassApprovesImmediately. requireLasting (internal/service/principal.go:25-30) has exactly 10 call sites: membership.go:112 (member suspend), :161 (Assign/RevokeRole), :218 (SetDefaultFlag); networks.go:228 (UpdatePolicy); gov_terms.go:67 (PublishTerms); closure_schedule.go:78/139/338; departure.go:39; erasure.go:88. It is absent from: createAdjustment (adjustments.go:79-115), setCreditLimit (membership.go:275-315), AdminResetPassword (recovery.go:326-397), ReverseTransaction (reversal.go:24-71), ResolveDispute (disputes_decide.go:33), DecideChallenge (challenges.go:162), DecideReReview (disputes_response.go:201), DecideJoinRequest (join.go:278), Create/RevokeInvitation (join.go:20/59), announcements (announcements.go:69/117), SuspendNetwork/ResumeNetwork (suspend.go:52/86). The web/API adapters add no break-glass restriction; the only break-glass page is the read-only history.

Extra probes (synthetic data): the default policy has DualControlThreshold=0 (policy.go:40-41). A break-glass admin alone posted one credit adjustment of MaxPolicyAmount (2^50 minor units) to another member, and that balance stayed spendable after the session expired. In the GOV-020 no-active-admin state, adjustments are refused (principal.go:124), but SetCreditLimit to 2^50 with no expiry, AdminResetPassword and SuspendNetwork still succeed and persist. Every existing break-glass test uses only reads as positive controls (audit2_regress_test.go:61-71, a3b_test.go:140-166), which matches the code's stated rule: "Such access must not leave lasting changes behind" (principal.go:18-19).

Excluded as not a defect: the bgAdmin early return at dualcontrol.go:27 is the accepted A3-01 exemption ("Break-glass administrators are not covered by this check", SEC-011-owner-decision.md:66). So the "approves the founder's 50,000.00 request immediately / no 24 h wait" sub-claim is permitted behaviour. The suggested fix of removing that early return would change an owner-approved rule and needs an owner decision.

Severity: not Critical or High. There is no auth bypass: a grant needs a deliberate operator CLI action as a System actor, with a live session of at most 4 h and a reason (breakglass.go:288-339). The grant is audited at platform and network scope and visible to admins and the grantee. Every action is audited under the member's identity, targets get notices (adjustments.go:161, membership.go:308, reversal.go:59, recovery.go:310), the blast radius is one network, and a permanent admin can post compensating entries. Password resets are limited to non-admin members with no other active network membership, at most 10 per hour (recovery.go:363-380, :25). It is more than Low: the effects outlive the session and are value-moving (unbounded minting under the default policy, persistent credit-limit raises, reversals, dispute outcomes) or hand over credentials (member-account takeover). That contradicts GOV-021 (P0), ARC-009 and the code's own invariant, and the owner-facing doc reports this as fixed. It is the same class as SA2-04 and A3-02b, both rated Medium. The password-reset item is the weakest part, since SEC-008 (09-security-privacy.md:197) permits operator resets under break-glass.
impact.spec_basis: GOV-021 (docs/specs/10-governance-operations.md:269, P0): during break-glass recovery the operator "MUST NOT change balances as part of recovery" and "MUST NOT appoint an administrator on its own authority". 10-governance-operations.md:64: the operator "does not decide network disputes". ARC-009 (docs/specs/05-architecture.md:181): "Read-only access MUST be the default". The code's own invariant: principal.go:18-19 and the requireLasting comment at principal.go:23-24. The SEC-013 addendum sets the grant as the full admin role (decision 7, docs/specs/addenda/SEC-013.md:16) and leaves narrowing open to the owner (Not done #4, SEC-013.md:39). SEC-011-owner-decision.md:59 states that A3-02 refuses break-glass administrators "for lasting actions". Accepted carve-out: A3-01's break-glass exemption from the grant-chain check and the 24 h wait (SEC-011-owner-decision.md:66), so dualcontrol.go:27 conforms.
impact.known: Partly known, and not fixed at this SHA for the residual paths. SEC-013 addendum "Not done" #4 (docs/specs/addenda/SEC-013.md:39) records that a break-glass admin can use all administrator powers and asks the owner whether to narrow this; it is open (owner-pending). SA2-04 (docs/audit/SECURITY-AUDIT-2.md:26, Medium) is fixed only for AssignRole, RevokeRole and UpdatePolicy. A3-02b (docs/audit/SECURITY-AUDIT-3.md:26, Medium) is fixed only for close, admin depart, non-self anonymise, member suspend and SetDefaultFlag; PublishTerms and closure schedule, cancel and verify also carry requireLasting at this SHA. The adjustment, limit, reversal, password-reset, dispute and challenge, join, invitation, announcement and network-suspension paths are not recorded as open in any audit table, and SEC-011-owner-decision.md:59 overstates A3-02 as refusing all lasting actions. The dual-control exemption is documented and accepted (SEC-011-owner-decision.md:66, A3-01).
